chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Abu Ishaq al-Sayqal, from Abu Yahya al-Razi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He (the Imam) asked: 'When a child is born to you, what do you do with it?' I said: 'I do not know what is done with it.' He said: 'Take a spoonful of gavshir (a type of vinegar or sour liquid), moisten it with water, then drip two drops into its right nostril and one drop into the left. Recite the Adhan in its right ear and the Iqamah in its left. Do this before the umbilical cord is cut, for it will not be startled ever, and the 'Mother of Children' (a type of child fever/illness) will not afflict it.'

key_terms.أَقِمْ: Recite the Iqamah (second call to prayer)
key_terms.أُمُّ الصِّبْيَانِ: Umm al-Sibyan, a specific childhood fever or illness
key_terms.جَاوَشِيرَ: Gavshir, a sour liquid or vinegar used in traditional remedies

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended rituals for a newborn in Shia tradition according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* prescribes the ritual of applying a mixture of *gavshir* (likely a resinous substance) to the newborn's nostrils and reciting the Adhan and Iqamah in the right and left ears respectively, prior to the cutting of the umbilical cord. In Shia tradition, these acts serve to imprint divine remembrance upon the child and provide spiritual protection against *Umm al-Sibyan*, a term often interpreted as either a specific childhood ailment or a jinnous entity affecting infants.
